problem: Prior world-model navigation was limited to toy scenes, and differentiable-rendering (NeRF-style) control work lacked real-time pose tracking and quantitative large-scale navigation evaluation, since pose estimation by backpropagating through the renderer is slow.
motivation: Differentiable rendering gives high-fidelity 3D world models, which are natural for planning, but vision-based navigation with them needs fast state estimation under noisy dynamics. The authors observe that TSDF-fusion style tracking (photometric + point-to-plane ICP) can be transplanted to voxel-grid differentiably-rendered maps, avoiding gradients through the renderer.
key_idea: Plan with A* in a learned voxel-grid occupancy world model and track the pose in real time by aligning the new RGB-D frame to the model-rendered previous frame with photometric + point-to-plane losses plus a dynamics prior.
insight: Anchoring observations to the map via the rendered previous frame is essential: the 'no map' ablation (frame-to-frame alignment) and dynamics-only integration both drop SPL to about 0.61 at low noise vs 0.92. The prediction-to-observation tracker matches emission-based tracking accuracy (location RMSE <0.1m in >99% of trajectories) but is about 4x faster (0.06s vs 0.25s). Voxel-grid rendering (0.05s) is also far faster than NeRF (2.72s), which enables online control.
method: Voxel-grid world model: occupancy and colour 3D tensors with trilinear interpolation; ray-surface intersection by linearising occupancy at the first threshold crossing; Laplace likelihood over RGB-D pixels; learned offline from 5000 pose-labelled RGB-D images.

A* motion planning: 2D grid over the occupancy model slice, 8-connected steps of 0.8 body length, collision check along each edge and a 1.2x body-length safety distance to obstacles, Euclidean heuristic.
Low-level controller: picks the nearest waypoint, rotates in place if heading error >5deg, else moves forward under max speed and angular velocity limits.

State estimator (MAP filter): the emission term is replaced by a photometric + point-to-plane ICP loss between the model-rendered previous-step image and the current observation, plus a dynamics-prior term on SE(3)/se(3) pose.
Optimisation details: 100 Adam steps per time step, 1000 sampled pixels, robust L1 with error thresholding, normals from rendered-depth gradients, projective data association.
Noisy-dynamics benchmark: clipped Gaussian noise on angular velocity and speed in Vizdoom, three noise levels, on six HouseExpo-based floor-plan levels.

setting.backbone: Voxel-grid occupancy/colour map (optimised per scene) + A* planner + hand-designed controller + ICP-style tracker
setting.training_data: Per-scene map fit on 5000 pose-labelled RGB-D images (sampled from the free space); no other training
setting.observation: RGB-D images (320x240 in Vizdoom) plus known start pose; no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: continuous angular velocity, movement direction and speed (max 11.5deg/step turn, 0.8 body length/step)
setting.simulator: Vizdoom (six HouseExpo floor-plan levels); qualitative AI2-THOR
setting.privileged: Known starting pose; per-scene map built from pose-labelled images; GT scene geometry used for collision checking and obstacle definition in Vizdoom

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 environments x 200 tasks, average over environments
numbers.backbone: voxel-grid world model + A* + point-to-plane tracker
numbers.extra: Per-scene map from 5000 pose-labelled images; sigma_a=3deg, sigma_s=10% of agent size; success if within 2x body length

numbers_note: Not a standard benchmark; the custom Vizdoom benchmark reports SPL only in a table (SPL≈SR per text). Values were printed as fractions and converted to percent.
results: Achieves 0.92 SPL (abstract: up to 92% success) at low noise, 0.79 mid and 0.46 high, versus 0.61/0.52/0.33 for the best ablated baselines (no-map tracking, dynamics only). Runs at about 16 Hz overall.
limitations: Evaluated mainly in low-fidelity Vizdoom with synthetic noise; AI2-THOR only qualitative
Requires an offline map built from pose-labelled images and a known start pose; performance degrades at high noise
Planar robot only; simple dynamics and controller; no dynamic obstacles
builds_on: Variational SLAM with differentiable voxel rendering (Mirchev et al. 2021)
